12: pin_project! {
13:     /// A future to write some of the buffer to an `AsyncWrite`.
14:     #[derive(Debug)]
15:     #[must_use = "futures do nothing unless you `.await` or poll them"]
16:     pub struct WriteAllBuf<'a, W: ?Sized, B> {
17:         writer: &'a mut W,
18:         buf: &'a mut B,
19:         #[pin]
20:         _pin: PhantomPinned,
21:     }
22: }
23: 
24: /// Tries to write some bytes from the given `buf` to the writer in an
25: /// asynchronous manner, returning a future.
26: pub(crate) fn write_all_buf<'a, W, B>(writer: &'a mut W, buf: &'a mut B) -> WriteAllBuf<'a, W, B>
27: where
28:     W: AsyncWrite + Unpin,
29:     B: Buf,
30: {
31:     WriteAllBuf {
32:         writer,
33:         buf,
34:         _pin: PhantomPinned,
35:     }
36: }
37: 
38: impl<'a, W> WriteAllBuf<'a, W, CopyBuffer>
39: where
40:     W: AsyncWrite + Unpin + ?Sized,
41: {
42:     pub(super) fn for_copy_buffer(writer: &'a mut W, buf: &'a mut CopyBuffer) -> Self {
43:         Self {
44:             writer,
45:             buf,
46:             _pin: PhantomPinned,
47:         }
48:     }
49: 
50:     pub(super) fn poll_copy<R>(
51:         &mut self,
52:         cx: &mut Context<'_>,
53:         mut reader: Pin<&mut R>,
54:     ) -> Poll<io::Result<u64>>
55:     where
56:         R: AsyncRead + ?Sized,
57:     {
58:         ready!(crate::trace::trace_leaf(cx));
59:         #[cfg(any(
60:             feature = "fs",
61:             feature = "io-std",
62:             feature = "net",
63:             feature = "process",
64:             feature = "rt",
65:             feature = "signal",
66:             feature = "sync",
67:             feature = "time",
68:         ))]
69:         // Keep track of task budget
70:         let coop = ready!(crate::runtime::coop::poll_proceed(cx));
71: 
72:         let writer = &mut *self.writer;
73:         let buffer = &mut *self.buf;
74: 
75:         loop {
76:             // If there is some space left in our buffer, then we try to read some
77:             // data to continue, thus maximizing the chances of a large write.
78:             if buffer.cap < buffer.buf.len() && !buffer.read_done {
79:                 let mut read_buf = ReadBuf::new(&mut buffer.buf);
80:                 read_buf.set_filled(buffer.cap);
81:                 match reader.as_mut().poll_read(cx, &mut read_buf) {
82:                     Poll::Ready(Ok(())) => {
83:                         let filled_len = read_buf.filled().len();
84:                         buffer.read_done = buffer.cap == filled_len;
85:                         buffer.cap = filled_len;
86:                         #[cfg(any(
87:                             feature = "fs",
88:                             feature = "io-std",
89:                             feature = "net",
90:                             feature = "process",
91:                             feature = "rt",
92:                             feature = "signal",
93:                             feature = "sync",
94:                             feature = "time",
95:                         ))]
96:                         coop.made_progress();
97:                     }
98:                     Poll::Ready(Err(err)) => {
99:                         #[cfg(any(
100:                             feature = "fs",
101:                             feature = "io-std",
102:                             feature = "net",
103:                             feature = "process",
104:                             feature = "rt",
105:                             feature = "signal",
106:                             feature = "sync",
107:                             feature = "time",
108:                         ))]
109:                         coop.made_progress();
110:                         return Poll::Ready(Err(err));
111:                     }
112:                     Poll::Pending => {
113:                         // Ignore pending reads when our buffer is not empty, because
114:                         // we can try to write data immediately.
115:                         if buffer.pos == buffer.cap {
116:                             // Try flushing when the reader has no progress to avoid deadlock
117:                             // when the reader depends on buffered writer.
118:                             if buffer.need_flush {
119:                                 ready!(Pin::new(&mut *writer).poll_flush(cx))?;
120:                                 #[cfg(any(
121:                                     feature = "fs",
122:                                     feature = "io-std",
123:                                     feature = "net",
124:                                     feature = "process",
125:                                     feature = "rt",
126:                                     feature = "signal",
127:                                     feature = "sync",
128:                                     feature = "time",
129:                                 ))]
130:                                 coop.made_progress();
131:                                 buffer.need_flush = false;
132:                             }
133: 
134:                             return Poll::Pending;
135:                         }
136:                     }
137:                 }
138:             }
139: 
140:             // If our buffer has some data, let's write it out!
141:             while buffer.pos < buffer.cap {
142:                 let i = match Pin::new(&mut *writer)
143:                     .poll_write(cx, &buffer.buf[buffer.pos..buffer.cap])
144:                 {
145:                     Poll::Pending => {
146:                         // Top up the buffer towards full if we can read a bit more
147:                         // data - this should improve the chances of a large write
148:                         if !buffer.read_done && buffer.cap < buffer.buf.len() {
149:                             let mut read_buf = ReadBuf::new(&mut buffer.buf);
150:                             read_buf.set_filled(buffer.cap);
151:                             ready!(reader.as_mut().poll_read(cx, &mut read_buf))?;
152:                             let filled_len = read_buf.filled().len();
153:                             buffer.read_done = buffer.cap == filled_len;
154:                             buffer.cap = filled_len;
155:                         }
156:                         return Poll::Pending;
157:                     }
158:                     Poll::Ready(Ok(n)) => n,
159:                     Poll::Ready(Err(err)) => return Poll::Ready(Err(err)),
160:                 };
161:                 #[cfg(any(
162:                     feature = "fs",
163:                     feature = "io-std",
164:                     feature = "net",
165:                     feature = "process",
166:                     feature = "rt",
167:                     feature = "signal",
168:                     feature = "sync",
169:                     feature = "time",
170:                 ))]
171:                 coop.made_progress();
172:                 if i == 0 {
173:                     return Poll::Ready(Err(io::Error::new(
174:                         io::ErrorKind::WriteZero,
175:                         "write zero byte into writer",
176:                     )));
177:                 } else {
178:                     buffer.pos += i;
179:                     buffer.amt += i as u64;
180:                     buffer.need_flush = true;
181:                 }
182:             }
183: 
184:             // If pos larger than cap, this loop will never stop.
185:             // In particular, user's wrong poll_write implementation returning
186:             // incorrect written length may lead to thread blocking.
187:             debug_assert!(
188:                 buffer.pos <= buffer.cap,
189:                 "writer returned length larger than input slice"
190:             );
191: 
192:             // All data has been written, the buffer can be considered empty again
193:             buffer.pos = 0;
194:             buffer.cap = 0;
195: 
196:             // If we've written all the data and we've seen EOF, flush out the
197:             // data and finish the transfer.
198:             if buffer.read_done {
199:                 ready!(Pin::new(&mut *writer).poll_flush(cx))?;
200:                 #[cfg(any(
201:                     feature = "fs",
202:                     feature = "io-std",
203:                     feature = "net",
204:                     feature = "process",
205:                     feature = "rt",
206:                     feature = "signal",
207:                     feature = "sync",
208:                     feature = "time",
209:                 ))]
210:                 coop.made_progress();
211:                 return Poll::Ready(Ok(buffer.amt));
212:             }
213:         }
214:     }
215: }
216: 
217: impl<W, B> Future for WriteAllBuf<'_, W, B>
218: where
219:     W: AsyncWrite + Unpin,
220:     B: Buf,
221: {
222:     type Output = io::Result<()>;
223: 
224:     fn poll(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<io::Result<()>> {
225:         let me = self.project();
226:         while me.buf.has_remaining() {
227:             let n = ready!(Pin::new(&mut *me.writer).poll_write(cx, me.buf.chunk())?);
228:             me.buf.advance(n);
229:             if n == 0 {
230:                 return Poll::Ready(Err(io::ErrorKind::WriteZero.into()));
231:             }
232:         }
233: 
234:         Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
235:     }
236: }

Implemented vectored `write_all_buf` support in `tokio/src/io/util/write_all_buf.rs`.

- Uses `Buf::chunks_vectored` with an eight-element `IoSlice` array when `AsyncWrite::is_write_vectored()` is true.
- Calls `poll_write_vectored` in that case; retains existing scalar `poll_write` behavior otherwise.
- Preserves partial-write handling and `WriteZero` detection.

Validated with:

```sh
docker exec cli-eval-opencode-tokio-rs__tokio-6724-de839be7 sh -lc 'cd /testbed && PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH cargo test -p tokio --features full --test io_write_all_buf'
```

All 3 relevant tests pass, including `write_all_buf_vectored`. `git diff --check` also passes.
